scope: Audit and qualify a digest-equivalent SHA-256 candidate; accept runtime changes only with measured support.
candidate: ring 0.17.14 SHA-256 versus existing sha2 0.11.0; same dependency versions as workspace
repeats: Predeclared for every micro group and any later full-operation group; retain all samples, including adverse results and spread above 5%.
correctness: Known SHA-256 vectors, padding/block/chunk boundary differential checks, independent Python hashlib oracles; native and QEMU CPU-masked checks. QEMU is correctness only, never performance evidence for physical CPUs without SHA-NI.
promotion_gate: A microbenchmark improvement must survive frozen full-publication/recovery and CLI comparisons. No skipped read/hash/comparison, zero shortcut, altered chunk size, cancellation or persistence gate.
if_promising: Privately build a candidate using ring only for bulk owned/retained payload hashing; retain SHA-256 identity/journal/TLS contracts. Qualify workspace and actual CLI fixtures, frozen native normal/reconciliation/attestation/acknowledgment controls, and whole recovery CLI. Restore production if full-operation results do not support promotion.
measurement_conditions: Serial workloads; no concurrent builds/tests/traces/plots; fixed CPU affinity; warm normal page cache; record CPU features and storage; host SMT/load/frequency not isolated. Distinguish wall, CPU and lifetime peak RSS.
